name: OWASP crAPI (completely ridiculous API)
intendedUse: Describes itself as vulnerable by design, for learning API security (README).
imageNote: The compose file at v1.1.6 uses ${VERSION:-latest}; no image carries a v1.1.6 tag, so the latest digests resolved on 2026-10-22 (last pushed 2025-09-22, the tag date) are pinned. postgres:14 and mongo:4.4 are moving tags. The web/gateway entry point is port 8888. Mailhog and the chatbot need outbound access and are left out under isolation.
builtBy: Claude (AI-assisted) from docs/challenges.md and the service source at the pinned commit; to be checked by labeller A before registration. The three undocumented "secret challenges" are not listed.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 1: Access details of another user’s vehicle
vulnerabilities.description: Vehicle location API returns any vehicle by its UUID.
vulnerabilities.note: The id is a UUID found through another API, not a guessable number.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 2: Access mechanic reports of other users
vulnerabilities.description: Mechanic report endpoint returns any report by its sequential numeric id.
vulnerabilities.note: Routes are defined in Java (identity), Go (community) or Python (workshop); Penthera reads routes from JS/TS only.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 3: Reset the password of a different user
vulnerabilities.description: Password-reset OTP can be brute-forced on an older API version.
vulnerabilities.note: Penthera’s rate-limit check covers login, not OTP verification.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 4: Find an API endpoint that leaks sensitive information of other users
vulnerabilities.description: Community posts API returns other users’ details.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 5: Find an API endpoint that leaks an internal property of a video
vulnerabilities.description: Video API returns an internal conversion property.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 6: Perform a layer 7 DoS using ‘contact mechanic’ feature
vulnerabilities.description: Contact-mechanic repeat parameter causes a request storm.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 7: Delete a video of another user
vulnerabilities.description: Admin video-delete endpoint is callable by a normal user.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 8: Get an item for free
vulnerabilities.description: Order update accepts a status field from the client.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 9: Increase your balance by $1,000 or more
Challenge 11: Make crAPI send an HTTP call to an external site
vulnerabilities.description: Contact-mechanic forwards a client-supplied URL from the server.
vulnerabilities.note: Routes are defined in Java (identity), Go (community) or Python (workshop); Penthera reads routes from JS/TS only. Under network isolation the outbound call cannot succeed; a scanner sees SSRF only through response differences.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 12: Find a way to get free coupons without knowing the coupon code
vulnerabilities.description: Coupon validation passes a JSON query object to MongoDB.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 13: Redeem an already claimed coupon by modifying the database
vulnerabilities.description: Apply-coupon builds SQL from the coupon_code field.
vulnerabilities.note: Routes are defined in Java (identity), Go (community) or Python (workshop); Penthera reads routes from JS/TS only.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 14: Find an endpoint that does not perform authentication checks
vulnerabilities.description: An order-details endpoint answers without a token although the API spec requires one.
vulnerabilities.note: Routes are defined in Java (identity), Go (community) or Python (workshop); Penthera reads routes from JS/TS only. The endpoint is inferred from source and the OpenAPI spec; the challenge text does not name it.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 15: Find a way to forge valid JWT tokens
vulnerabilities.description: Identity service JWT verification is weak (algorithm confusion, unchecked signature on one route, kid traversal).
vulnerabilities.note: Routes are defined in Java (identity), Go (community) or Python (workshop); Penthera reads routes from JS/TS only. Several documented sub-flaws share this one entry; the jku variant needs an attacker-hosted key and is out-of-band.

vulnerabilities.title: Challenge 16: Use the chatbot to do a successful prompt injection
Challenge 17: Extract the credentials of another user using chatbot
Challenge 18: Make the chatbot do an action on behalf of another user
vulnerabilities.description: Chatbot performs actions for another user.
